Case FilesFIG. 03 — SELECTED WORK

Six projects, one recurring habit: build the tool before the feature.

Each entry below is a shipped or in-flight project with its own scope, constraints and outcome — from a two-person indie horror comedy to a Defence Force-grade simulator.

Case File — 01 / Current

Spooker

In Development
Technical Lead & Sole Engineer — Space Dragon Games

A horror roguelite pool-like where every shot counts and every mistake could be your last. Across a smoke-drenched speakeasy that keeps twisting into stranger, harder tables, precise billiards meets escalating roguelite risk — chase combo chains and towering multipliers, or lose it all in an instant, all scored to a live-recorded big band swing soundtrack. Ralphie, the speakeasy's last remaining regular, isn't in a hurry to let you leave.

As the only engineer on a three-person core team, responsible for the vast majority of the code and every platform's maintenance — targeting simultaneous release across PC, Mac, Linux, PlayStation, Xbox, Switch and Mobile.

Also owns extreme performance optimization work, chasing Steam Deck Verified status by roughly halving the game's GPU frame cost, and runs delivery through Simply Ship — an in-house CI/CD tool built to give the studio full control over its release pipeline.

Case File — 02

Reave

Shipped — Quest & PCVR
Senior Unity Developer — Alta VR

A dark fantasy VR action game built across three years for Quest 2, Quest 3, Quest 3s and PCVR. Owned the enemy-facing half of combat: a custom, scalable, multiplayer-ready AI state machine system driving encounter behaviour, alongside physical sword, melee and projectile combat designed to hold up in both PvE and PvP.

Also authored the networked stat system, handled performance optimization passes, and integrated third-party tooling including LIV, VContainer for dependency injection, and R3 for reactive state.

Case File — 03

Gods Unchained

Shipped — Live Service
Senior Unity Developer — Immutable, Sydney

Nearly three years on Immutable's trading card game, spanning a fully visual-scripted, no-code test suite, two tutorial systems built for non-engineers to author, and the game's Network Reconnect architecture.

The test suite let QA write playmode tests as visual graphs with zero code and no compilation step — Unity's own engineering team confirmed no other studio had built anything comparable on their engine. It scaled the team from 150 to 3,500 tests in under six months.

Also engineered the API and logging layer behind the Twitch integration with Cardboard Live, letting viewers inspect card history and purchase cards directly from a live stream — and stayed a primary community point of contact across streams, podcasts and tournaments.

3,500+Automated Tests
<15 minFull Suite Runtime
<2 secPer Playmode Test
Tutorial System Cardboard Live Extension Trial of the Gods Trailer
150 → 3,500

Tests scaled 23x in under six months once QA could write playmode tests as no-code visual graphs — each one resolving in under two seconds, with the full suite finishing in under fifteen minutes. Unity's own team called it a potential industry-leading approach for the engine.

Case File — 04

Defence Simulation & XR — DXC Technology

2017 – 2019
Graduate Engineer → Technical Lead

Started as a graduate learning from simulation-industry veterans on the ANZAC Navy Simulations Project, then led performance testing, server design, documentation and research for MOBOTS — a project aimed at shrinking deployed ship-simulation servers into a far smaller, more affordable footprint.

Led development of a mobile marksmanship trainer for the Australian Army, accurately modelling bullet drop, wind resistance, planetary rotation, scope zeroing, night/thermal vision and the effect of breathing on aim — and led the AR companion app for the Royal Australian Air Force's Avalon Airshow, letting attendees scan and "collect" real aircraft in AR.

On a restricted-client HoloLens + VR project, helped push photogrammetry and on-device rendering to turn hundreds of gigabytes of photography into scanned, textured models in real time over a custom netstack — synced via a secured database and a custom SFTP/Docker delivery pipeline. Represented the project at the HoloLens 2 launch in Seattle.

Unannounced Title

Senior Game Developer — Amplitude – Sega Studios

Nothing playable can be shown — the project remains unreleased. What can be shared: the team ran on strict extreme-programming principles, writing all gameplay code test-first before ever wiring it to a MonoBehaviour, with every change peer-programmed and continuously reviewed.

Tooling & Open SourceFIG. 04 — INFRASTRUCTURE

Built once, reused on every project since.

A running habit across every role above: when the pipeline doesn't exist, build it. These two tools now sit under every release of Spooker.

Simply Ship

An in-house CI/CD tool for tailoring an exact multi-platform delivery pipeline to a small studio's needs — currently driving every build and release of Spooker across seven target platforms.

View on GitHub

Simply Log

A companion logging system built alongside Simply Ship, designed to keep build and release activity readable and traceable across every platform in the pipeline.

View on GitHub
